questions.question: Which of the following public sector enterprises falls under the status ‘Maharatna’?
questions.solution: Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) is categorized as a Maharatna company. These are PSUs with high financial autonomy and significant global presence.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.solution: The incorrect pair is Airport Authority of India (AAI) – Navratna. AAI is actually classified as a Miniratna enterprise.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of public sector industry in India?
questions.solution: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) is a public sector industry, meaning it is owned and managed by the government. The other options are private sector companies.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of private sector industry in India?
questions.solution: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO/Tata Steel) is a prime example of a private sector industry, founded by Jamsetji Tata in 1907.

questions.question:
Correctly match the following:
1. Public sector | a. TISCO
2. Private sector | b. BHEL
3. Joint sector | c. Oil India Ltd
questions.solution: The correct sequence is: BHEL (Public Sector), TISCO (Private Sector), and Oil India Ltd (Joint Sector).

questions.question: Which of the following is a joint sector industry in India?
questions.solution: Oil India Limited (OIL) is a joint sector industry, which involves ownership and operation by both the state and private individuals/groups.

questions.question:
Identify which of the following statements are correct.
1. Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) was incorporated on 9 November 1967.
2. The Khetri Copper Complex (KCC) is located in Rajasthan.
3. The headquarters of Mineral Exploration Consultancy Ltd. is located in Jaipur.
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because the headquarters of Mineral Exploration Consultancy Ltd. is located in Nagpur, not Jaipur.

questions.question: ONGC _____ is a subsidiary of the Indian public sector enterprise, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation.
questions.solution: ONGC Videsh is the international subsidiary of ONGC, focusing on acquiring oil and gas acreage outside India to ensure the nation's energy security.

questions.question: What role did the WTO membership (1995) play in India's post-reform globalization strategy?
questions.option_2: Deepened India's integration into global trade
questions.solution: Joining the WTO in 1995 required India to lower tariffs and remove trade barriers. This significantly deepened India's integration into the global economy, facilitating better market access and attracting foreign investment.

questions.question: Which of the following institutions conducts the survey on employment and unemployment?
questions.option_2: National Institution of Economic and Social Research
questions.option_3: National Council of Applied Economic Research
questions.solution: The National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) is the primary body in India responsible for conducting large-scale socio-economic surveys, including those on employment and unemployment.

questions.question: The analysis of the interrelationship between the economy and the environment in the economic environmental accounting system was put forward by______ .
questions.solution: The United Nations Statistical Office developed the System of Environmental Economic Accounting (SEEA) to measure how the environment contributes to the economy and how economic activity impacts the environment.

questions.question: Which of the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) seeks to ‘Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss’?
questions.solution: SDG 15 (Life on Land) aims to sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt biodiversity loss. SDG 12 focuses on sustainable consumption, and SDG 7 on affordable energy.

questions.question: The UN’s Sustainable Development Goal 6 aims to ______.
questions.option_1: ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages
questions.option_2: ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all
questions.option_3: end poverty in all forms everywhere
questions.option_4: take urgent action to combat climate change and its impact
questions.solution: SDG 6 is dedicated to ensuring clean water and sanitation for all. In contrast, SDG 1 aims to end poverty and SDG 13 addresses climate change.

questions.question: The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) focuses on:
questions.option_1: Developing industrial clusters in backward regions
questions.solution: Launched by NITI Aayog in 2018, the Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) targets 112 socio-economically underdeveloped districts to improve their status through health, education, and infrastructure development.

questions.question: The PM-MITRA scheme is focused on which of the following objectives?
questions.option_2: Enhancing textile exports and setting up large textile parks
questions.option_4: Providing smart classrooms in rural schools
questions.solution: The PM-MITRA (Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel) scheme aims to build world-class textile parks to integrate the entire textile value chain, boosting exports and global competitiveness.

questions.question: Which government scheme aims to phase out unfit and polluting vehicles from India's roads to reduce emissions and boost automotive industry recycling?
questions.solution: The Voluntary Vehicle Fleet Modernisation Programme (also called the Scrappage Policy) was launched in 2021 to remove old, polluting vehicles and encourage the use of modern, eco-friendly transport.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.option_1: Mission Shakti - Startup grants for rural men
questions.option_2: PM-AAGY - Railway safety in backward areas
questions.solution: Swadesh Darshan 2.0 is correctly matched as it focuses on developing theme-based tourist circuits. Mission Shakti is for women's empowerment, and PM-JANMAN focuses on tribal development (primarily rural).

questions.question: Which of the following schemes provides annual income support to farmers directly into their bank accounts?
questions.solution: PM-KISAN provides eligible farmer families with ₹6,000 per year in three equal installments through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

questions.question: What is the central objective of Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 scheme?
questions.option_1: Strengthening early childhood care and nutrition delivery systems
questions.solution: Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 aims to address malnutrition and improve early childhood care through modernized Anganwadis and better nutrition delivery for women and children.

questions.question: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs?
questions.option_1: Social mobilisation, economic development, and education
questions.option_2: Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
questions.option_3: Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
questions.option_4: Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building of the poor
questions.solution: The South Asia Poverty Alleviation Programme (SAPAP) model focuses on three pillars: Social mobilisation (organizing the poor), Capital formation (savings), and Capacity building (skill training).

questions.question: Which of the following is the main objective of the DWCRA model of SHGs?
questions.option_1: To provide education opportunities for rural children
questions.option_2: To provide housing support for rural families
questions.option_3: To provide self-employment opportunities for rural women
questions.option_4: To provide healthcare services to rural women
questions.solution: The DWCRA (Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas) scheme was launched to create self-employment opportunities specifically for rural women in BPL households.

questions.question: When was the Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) announced by India?
questions.solution: The DFTP scheme was announced in 2008. India was the first developing nation to provide duty-free market access to Least Developed Countries (LDCs) to support their trade.

questions.question: When was the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) introduced to provide health insurance to people below the poverty line?
questions.solution: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) was launched in 2008 to provide BPL households with health insurance for hospitalisation expenses.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act of 2006 in India?
questions.option_2: To focus on large-scale industries only
questions.option_3: To increase import tariffs to protect MSMEs
questions.option_4: To promote and facilitate the development of MSMEs
questions.solution: The MSMED Act, 2006 was enacted specifically to promote and facilitate the growth of micro, small, and medium enterprises by defining them and establishing a supportive legal framework.

questions.question: The RBI launched the Lead Bank Scheme (LBS) to mobilise deposits and step-up lending to weaker sections of the economy. When was the scheme launched?
questions.solution: The Lead Bank Scheme (LBS) was introduced in 1969 based on the Gadgil and Nariman Committee reports. It assigns a specific bank as the 'Lead Bank' for a district to coordinate credit delivery.
